components:
  schemas:
    ProblemDetail:
      title: Problem Detail
      description: The schema for all error responses.
      type: object
      properties:
        type:
          title: Type
          description: Full URL that originated the error response.
          type: string
          format: uri
          example: 'http://localhost:9966/petclinic/api/owner'
          readOnly: true
        title:
          title: Title
          description: The short error title.
          type: string
          example: NoResourceFoundException
          readOnly: true
        status:
          title: Status
          description: HTTP status code
          type: integer
          format: int32
          minimum: 400
          maximum: 600
          exclusiveMaximum: true
          example: 500
          readOnly: true
        detail:
          title: Detail
          description: The long error message.
          type: string
          example: 'No static resource api/owner.'
          readOnly: true
        timestamp:
          title: Timestamp
          description: The time the error occurred.
          type: string
          format: date-time
          example: '2024-11-23T13:59:21.3820407Z'
          readOnly: true
        schemaValidationErrors:
          title: Schema validation errors
          description: Validation errors against the OpenAPI schema.
          type: array
          items:
            $ref: '#/components/schemas/ValidationMessage'
      required:
        - type
        - title
        - status
        - detail
        - timestamp
        - schemaValidationErrors
    ValidationMessage:
      title: Validation message
      description: Messages describing a validation error.
      type: object
      properties:
        message:
          title: Message
          description: The validation message.
          type: string
          example: "[Path '/lastName'] Instance type (null) does not match any allowed primitive type (allowed: ['string'])"
          readOnly: true
      required:
        - message
      additionalProperties: true
    Specialty:
      title: Specialty
      description: Fields of specialty of vets.
      type: object
      properties:
        id:
          title: ID
          description: The ID of the specialty.
          type: integer
          format: int32
          minimum: 0
          example: 1
          readOnly: true
        name:
          title: Name
          description: The name of the specialty.
          type: string
          maxLength: 80
          minLength: 1
          example: radiology
      required:
        - id
        - name
    OwnerFields:
      title: Owner fields
      description: Editable fields of a pet owner.
      type: object
      properties:
        title:
          title: Title
          description: >-
            The optional honorific title of the pet owner (typically one of
            'MR', 'MRS', 'MS' or 'DR'). When present it is used to compose the
            owner's 'salutation'.
          type: string
          maxLength: 10
          example: DR
        firstName:
          title: First name
          description: The first name of the pet owner.
          type: string
          minLength: 1
          maxLength: 30
          pattern: "^[\\p{L}]+([ '-][\\p{L}]+){0,2}$"
          example: George
          x-field-extra-annotation: "@jakarta.validation.constraints.NotBlank"
        lastName:
          title: Last name
          description: The last name of the pet owner.
          type: string
          minLength: 1
          maxLength: 30
          pattern: "^[\\p{L}]+([ '-][\\p{L}]+){0,2}\\.?$"
          example: Franklin
          x-field-extra-annotation: "@jakarta.validation.constraints.NotBlank"
        address:
          title: Address
          description: >-
            The flat postal address of the pet owner. Accepted for backward
            compatibility; prefer the structured 'addressLine1'/'addressLine2'
            fields. When structured fields are supplied they take precedence and
            the returned 'address' is composed from them. Optional at the schema
            level: an owner is valid when it supplies an address in either form
            (a non-blank 'addressLine1' or this flat 'address') plus a city.
          type: string
          maxLength: 255
          example: '110 W. Liberty St.'
        addressLine1:
          title: Address line 1
          description: >-
            The first line of the owner's structured postal address. When present
            (non-blank) it is preferred over the flat 'address', is normalized the
            same way, and forms the composed 'address' returned in the response.
          type: string
          maxLength: 255
          example: '110 W. Liberty St.'
        addressLine2:
          title: Address line 2
          description: >-
            The optional second line of the owner's structured postal address
            (unit, suite, etc.). When present it is normalized and appended to the
            normalized 'addressLine1', separated by a single space, to form the
            composed 'address'.
          type: string
          maxLength: 255
          example: 'Unit 4'

## Summary

I changed owner deletion from a hard delete to a soft delete across the Spring layers:

**Domain model** — `Owner.java`: added a `deleted` boolean field (`@Column(name = "deleted")`) with `isDeleted()`/`setDeleted()`. A newly created owner defaults to `false`.

**Persistence schema** — added a `deleted BOOLEAN DEFAULT FALSE NOT NULL` column to the `owners` table in all four DB schemas (`h2`, `hsqldb`, `mysql`, `postgres`). I put `DEFAULT` before `NOT NULL` because HSQLDB (the test profile's DB) rejects the reverse order.

**API contract** — `openapi.yml`: added a read-only `deleted` boolean property to the `Owner` schema, so the generated `OwnerDto` carries it and MapStruct auto-maps it from the entity. `GET /api/owners/{id}` now returns `deleted` (false for new, true after delete).

**Service layer** — `ClinicServiceImpl.java`:
- `deleteOwner(...)` now sets `deleted = true` and `save`s the owner instead of removing the row (returns 2xx, record retained). This is repository/profile-independent.
- Added a `findActiveOwners()` helper and routed the create endpoint's **duplicate and identity checks** through it — `findHouseholdMembers` (the 409-blocking household duplicate), `countNamesakes`, and `deduplicateCustomerCode` — so owners flagged `deleted` are ignored. A normally-blocking duplicate is now allowed when the only matching owner has been soft-deleted.

I intentionally left the daily-limit and city-capacity rules counting all rows, since those are capacity/rate limits rather than the duplicate/identity checks the spec scopes the change to.
